citation: Fancsali, C., Abe, Y., Pyatigorsky, M., Ortiz, L., Hunt, A., Chan, V., Saltares, E., Toby, M., Schellinger, A., & Jaciw, A. P. (2015). The Impact of the Reading Apprenticeship Improving Secondary Education (RAISE) Project on Academic Literacy in High School: A Report of a Randomized Experiment in Pennsylvania and California Schools (Empirical Education Rep. No. Empirical_RAISE-7019-FR1-O.2). Palo Alto, CA: Empirical Education Inc.
report_number: Empirical Education Rep. No. Empirical_RAISE-7019-FR1-O.2 (ERIC ED571000); i3 Validation grant U39B100255 to WestEd
design: Cluster RCT in the report itself (school-level random assignment, blocked); 42 schools randomized (22 treatment / 20 control), 252 teachers (130 T / 122 C); two waves (wave 1 = 32 schools in CA+PA, 2011; wave 2 = 10 CA schools, 2012). Intervention = Reading Apprenticeship discipline-specific TPD (65 hours / 10 days over 12 months) for ELA, science (biology), and U.S. history teachers; control = business as usual. Grades 9-12 (registry band 7-12). Outcome = ETS scenario-based disciplinary literacy/reading-comprehension assessment (Reading for Understanding grant). Two-level HLM (students nested in schools), intent-to-treat, controlling for student 8th-grade state ELA/reading pretest z-scores, demographics (gender, race/ethnicity, ELL, special-ed, FRPL), school-level baseline state proficiency, and blocking variables. Year-2 analytic sample (all 42 schools, after full PD dose) = immediate post-treatment wave.
problems: DESIGN LABEL DISCREPANCY: the meta-analysis registry codes row 29 as 'QED' and 'Unpublished', but this report is explicitly a cluster RANDOMIZED controlled trial (i3 validation RCT, school-level random assignment with blocking; Methods p.8 and Appendix A). Author, year (Fancsali et al. 2015), grade band (9-12, registry 7-12), SES profile, and the 'Other'/'Reading' subject hints in the published fixture all match this RAISE final report, so this is almost certainly the correct source; the QED tag is likely the meta-analysts' own coding decision (possibly treating the post-attrition analytic sample, or the associated non-RCT 'scale-up study', as quasi-experimental). The report publishes both an RCT (extracted here) and a separate 'scale-up study' in non-RCT schools (not reported in this PDF). EFFECT SIZE METHOD: the report prints standardized 'Effect size' values directly (Table 13, p.45) computed as model-based impact (HLM treatment coefficient) divided by the unadjusted pooled SD of the standardized ETS score (raw SD = 0.937, p.45 note); this is the Empirical Education/WWC convention (a Hedges'-style g, not labeled g; small-sample J correction not applied but negligible, J>0.99 at these N). I record the report's printed effect sizes as g. g_se is derived as the reported impact SE (raw score units) divided by the same standardizing SD (0.937); g_var = g_se^2. ICC is NOT reported anywhere (only a design MDES of 0.16 full sample / 0.24 subgroups, p.48), so icc is left null; clustering is already handled by the two-level HLM so cluster_adjusted=true and central ICC re-correction is unnecessary. n_clusters = 42 schools for the full sample; the report does not break n_clusters down by subject-area class, so 42 is recorded for the by-subject rows as well (subject subsets draw teachers/students from the same 42 schools). Subject mapping: the outcome is a reading-comprehension/literacy assessment administered in three content-area classes; per spec (reading/literacy/ELA -> Reading) all literacy-assessment outcomes are mapped to Reading, with the content-class context noted. The science-class subset uses a biology-content reading assessment but the construct is reading/literacy, hence Reading. Timepoint = Year 2 (end of full treatment dose, full 42-school sample); Year 1, Year 3, and subgroup/state results are reported but not extracted as the primary post-treatment contrasts (Year-1 and Year-3 g's and subgroup g's noted below for reference).

effect_sizes.arm_label: Reading Apprenticeship (RAISE) TPD vs business-as-usual control (single TPD arm)
effect_sizes.test_name: ETS scenario-based disciplinary literacy assessment (Reading for Understanding), unidimensional score - full sample, all subjects combined
effect_sizes.timepoint: post, spring Year 2 (end of full 65-hour/10-day PD dose; full 42-school sample)
effect_sizes.g_method: Report's printed standardized effect size (Table 13): two-level HLM treatment coefficient (impact = 0.13, pretest/covariate-adjusted) divided by the unadjusted pooled SD of the standardized ETS score (raw SD = 0.937). Taken directly as g (WWC/Empirical Education convention; J correction negligible at this N). g_se = impact_se 0.100 / 0.937 = 0.1067; g_var = g_se^2.
effect_sizes.page_ref: p.45 Table 13 (row 'Literacy achievement assessment score'); also p.89 Table I2 ('Unidimensional Score'); exec summary p.6
effect_sizes.notes: Headline full-sample (all subjects combined) achievement result; positive but not statistically significant (p=.184). Total Year-2 analytic n = 10,173 students; report does not split this n into treatment vs control counts. Adjusted means -0.02 (T) / -0.16 (C). This composite subsumes the three by-subject subscale rows below. Improvement index 5.6%. Robust across alternative model specs (Table I3, g 0.11-0.16).

effect_sizes.notes: Subject-area subset (students in science classes) of the full sample; STATISTICALLY SIGNIFICANT (impact 0.31*, p=.010, improvement index 12.6%). Largest impact, attributed to RA representing a larger pedagogical shift for science teachers. Reading/literacy construct measured in science classes -> Reading per spec. n = 4,360 (combined T+C). Adjusted means 0.01 (T) / -0.29 (C). Robust across model specs (Table I3, g 0.29-0.32).
